div.head: III Eg 7.1
div.ab: Gyf he þonne ne mæge, gewylde man hine swaðor man mæge, swa cwicne swa deadne; ⁊ nime man eal þæt he age ⁊ gylde man þam teonde his ceapgyld ángeldes, ⁊ fo se landhlaford to healfan, to healfan þæt hundred.

Gyf he þonne ne mæge, gewylde mon hine swaðer man mæge, swa cucenne swa deadne; ⁊ niman eal þæt he age ⁊ gylde man þam teonde his cepgyld angyldes, ⁊ fó se hlaford elles to healfum, to healfan þæt hundred.

Gif he þonne ne mæge, gewylde hine mon swæðer man mæge, swa cucne swa deadne; ⁊ nime man eal þæt age ⁊ gylde man þam teonde his ceapgyld angyldes, ⁊ fo se hlaford elles to healfum, to healfan þæt hundred.

Si non possit, exsuperetur quibus modis poterit sic uiuus sic mortuus; et capiatur omne quod habebit, et reddatur repetenti captale suum semel, et reliquum habeat dominus dimidium, hundretus dimidium.

Gif he þonne ne mæge, gewilde man hine swa hwaðer swa man mæge, swa cucune swa deadne, ⁊ niman eal þæt he age, ⁊ gilde man ðam teondan his ceapgild angildes, ⁊ fo se hlaford elles to healfum, to healfum þæt hundred.

And if he cannot do so, they shall seize him as they can, either alive or dead, and they shall take all that he has, and shall pay to the accuser the unaugmented value of his goods; and the lord of the manor shall take half [of what remains], and the hundred half.

If, however, he cannot, one is to secure him however one can, alive or dead, and seize all that he owns, and pay to the accuser simple compensation for his goods, and the lord of the estate is to succeed to half, and the hundred to half.

Wenn er [dies] aber nicht kann, bemächtige man, wie man kann, sich seiner, lebend oder todt; und man nehme (sie nehmen A D) alles, was er hat, fort, und man zahle [davon] dem Kläger dessen Ersatzgeld einfach, und (vom Übrigen A D G2 Qu) greife zur Hälfte der (Grund-[Immunitäts-] G) Herr [des Verbrechers], zur Hälfte die Hundertschaft.

But if he cannot [do this], let him be overpowered however one can, alive or dead; and let everything he has be taken (let them take, A D), and let the plaintiff be paid [from it] his compensation once, and (of the rest, A D G2 Qu) let the (immunity-landlord, G) lord [of the criminal] take half, the hundred half.
div.note: ‘hlaford elles’ is the reading of A, D, G2 and Quadr.; Hu 2.1 has ‘hlaford’. Liebermann compares Hu 2.1; III Em 2; II As 20.4–6. G2: after ‘þæt’ supply ‘he’ (Liebermann).
The Wulfstan MSS and Cnut’s laws add the favourite Wulfstan word, elles “otherwise”.
